### Observed differences

- In the later window, the elapsed time between the completion of A04 and the following completion of A01 is longer: the median gap rose from about 25 hours to about 42 hours (mean from about 27 to about 46 hours), and the upper quartile from about 38 to about 66 hours, while the fastest cases stayed at a few minutes in both windows. The pair occurs in all 200 traces of each window. [TWAIT001]
- In the later window, work on A13 is concentrated on a single resource: earlier it was spread thinly over roughly 46 distinct resources, with the busiest handling about 7 in 100 A13 occurrences, whereas later one resource (User_134) handled all of them (concentration index about 0.03 to 1.0). Roughly 270 A13 occurrences back each window. [ASSIGN001, CONC001]
- In the later window, A22's assignments shifted to a largely different set of resources while staying dispersed: the busiest resource handled about 10 in 100 A22 occurrences earlier and about 8 in 100 later; several resources present earlier no longer appear, several new ones appear with roughly 4–7 in 100 each, and a few continue. About 120 occurrences per window. [ASSIGN002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that work was reallocated across resources while the control flow stayed intact. In the earlier window, A13 was handled by many different resources (about 46 distinct, the busiest with about 7 in 100 occurrences), whereas in the later window all A13 work was handled by one resource (User_134); A22 shows the same kind of reallocation in milder form, its work moving to a largely different set of resources while remaining dispersed. The signs are direct and consistent: the assignment-mix and concentration indicators show the A13 change from two angles, each backed by roughly 270 occurrences per window, and the resources family produced 3 qualifying items where about 0.006 would be expected if nothing had changed, with every item larger than in essentially all of 2,000 random re-splits. Limitations: the two A13 indicators describe one underlying behaviour rather than two independent confirmations, the evidence covers only A13 and A22, and no control-flow item qualified (0 against about 0.19 expected by chance), so the reallocation cannot be tied to any structural change. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, CONC001]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a difference in case mix between the windows: different kinds of cases could naturally use different resources and show longer A04-to-A01 gaps without any change in the process itself, and the evidence offers no case attributes to check this. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, CONC001, TWAIT001]

Other differences: A timing change stands on its own: the elapsed time between the completion of A04 and the following completion of A01 increased across the bulk of the distribution (median about 25 to about 42 hours, mean about 27 to about 46 hours, upper quartile about 38 to about 66 hours) while the fastest cases stayed at a few minutes; with 1 time item against about 0.014 expected by chance and the pair present in all 200 traces per window, this is a supported change in timing that needs no structural counterpart. [TWAIT001]
